The Supreme Court has held that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to a pollution-free environment.
Pollution Control Boards at the Centre and in the States enforce the Water and Air Acts.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on concept of sustainable development and answer the questions that follow.
"The Rio Earth Summit adopted the Rio Declaration and Agenda 21. Sustainable development balances economic growth, social development and environmental protection. India's Supreme Court has accepted sustainable development as part of the law of the land."
(i) The Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment was held in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Agenda 21' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The Stockholm Conference is a landmark. (2)
items.answer: (i) 1972 (ii) The action plan for sustainable development adopted at the Rio Earth Summit. (iii) It was the first major UN conference on the environment and led to UNEP.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 1972 (ii) The action plan for sustainable development adopted at the Rio Earth Summit. (iii) It was the first major UN conference on the environment and led to UNEP.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about concept of sustainable development:
I. The SDGs are to be achieved by 2050.
II. India's Supreme Court has accepted sustainable development as part of the law of the land.
III. Intergenerational equity requires the present generation to hold natural resources in trust for future generations.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II and III only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: They are to be achieved by 2030. II is correct. III is correct.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: National Green Tribunal Act – 2010
items.markingKey: (d) National Green Tribunal Act – 2010. Air Act – 1981; Water Act – 1974; Environment (Protection) Act – 1986 are the correct pairs for the others.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Development and environment must be balanced.
Reason (R): Economic growth that destroys the environment cannot be sustained.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: economic growth that destroys the environment cannot be sustained.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on principles of environmental jurisprudence and the NGT and answer the questions that follow.
"The NGT is guided by the principles of natural justice and not by the Code of Civil Procedure. The NGT applies sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle. The precautionary principle shifts the burden of proof to the person proposing an activity to show that it is environmentally benign."
(i) Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof is on the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'precautionary principle' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The polluter pays principle deters pollution. (2)
items.answer: (i) developer or industrialist (ii) The principle that lack of scientific certainty must not be used as a reason to postpone measures to prevent environmental degradation. (iii) The polluter must bear the full cost of the damage caused.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) developer or industrialist (ii) The principle that lack of scientific certainty must not be used as a reason to postpone measures to prevent environmental degradation. (iii) The polluter must bear the full cost of the damage caused.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about constitutional provisions and environmental statutes:
I. Article 48A is a fundamental right.
II. Protecting the environment is only the duty of the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Neither I nor II
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: It is a Directive Principle of State Policy. II is incorrect: Article 51A(g) makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen too.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about principles of environmental jurisprudence and the NGT:
I. The NGT is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure.
II. The public trust doctrine allows the State to sell rivers to private owners.
III. The precautionary principle shifts the burden of proof to the person proposing an activity to show that it is environmentally benign.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: III only
items.markingKey: (d) I is incorrect: It is guided by the principles of natural justice. II is incorrect: The State holds such resources in trust for the public. III is correct.

items.stem: The right to a clean environment has been read by the courts into:
items.answer: Article 21
items.markingKey: (b) Article 21.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Article 48A is a Directive Principle and Article 51A(g) is a fundamental duty. The Supreme Court has held that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to a pollution-free environment. The Environment (Protection) Act 1986 is an umbrella legislation covering water, air and land. The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 and the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 protect wildlife and forests."
(i) Explain the term 'Central Pollution Control Board', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Citizens can approach the courts for a clean environment. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Environment Protection Act was enacted in 1974." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The statutory body constituted under the Water Act 1974 to prevent and control water and air pollution. (ii) The courts have read the right to a healthy environment into Article 21. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was enacted in 1986; the Water Act was enacted in 1974.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The statutory body constituted under the Water Act 1974 to prevent and control water and air pollution. (ii) The courts have read the right to a healthy environment into Article 21. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It was enacted in 1986; the Water Act was enacted in 1974.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about principles of environmental jurisprudence and the NGT is correct?
items.answer: The NGT applies sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: The State holds such resources in trust for the public. It is guided by the principles of natural justice. Lack of certainty is no reason to postpone preventive measures.
options: The NGT is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure.
The public trust doctrine allows the State to sell rivers to private owners.
Under the precautionary principle, action is taken only after scientific certainty.
The NGT applies sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.
